import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I published the lead's report as the canonical `202610/sase_launch_post_reading_list/sase_launch_post_reading_list.md`, embedded the infographic, and registered it (`ref=file:explicit:23984e1f9af93d45959001b5`, label `research:202610/sase_launch_post_reading_list/sase_launch_post_reading_list.md`). The host commits it to the research repo after this turn ends. `__final.md` and the five drafts are unchanged.

**Layout.** The file opens with the title, then a one-sentence research query, then the infographic, then `## Bottom line`. After that come the reading-history review, the ranked list (15 items), what to pull forward from your library, the capture commands, reading for SASE itself, how the reports agreed and split, what was dropped, corrections to the individual reports, and method and limits.

**Edits:**
- **Headings:** I removed the hand-numbering. Each ranked item now has a plain-title heading, and its rank ("Rank #1") sits on the section's first line.
- **Byline and question:** The lead's byline and its own "Research question" restatement moved into "Method and limits".
- **Tables:** All five tables are now nested lists. A script confirmed every cell is still there except the headers of the columns that name each row, which the list format drops by design. pandoc finds no tables left.
- **Section references:** Because sections moved, I replaced "§5" and "#N below" references with links to the named section. References to your blog outline (§1.1, §1.3.1, §1.3.2, §1.5) are left as written.
- **Cross-links:** I added a few links between parts of the file, and all of them resolve when I build it with pandoc. The lead's report has no Mermaid diagrams, and none were added.

**Links:**
- All 54 distinct URLs from the lead's report are in the new file, and none were dropped or replaced.
- 53 load. The two Engelbart pages failed once and loaded on retry; they redirect to `dougengelbart.org/content/view/…` and I kept the lead's URLs.
- The ResearchGate copy of Klein et al. returns 403, so I kept it as unverified.
- The relative links to the five draft reports and to the infographic all resolve.
